transcript: Last night, I attended A Wonderful World, a new jukebox musical based on the life and career of Louis Armstrong, one of the most influential jazz musicians in history. The story is told in four chapters, each with its own location and each featuring one of Louis’s four wives. Like a lot of bio-jukebox musicals, it's not the deepest story but this production feels like it intends to be mostly a celebration of his music, which it definitely accomplishes. The scenes are quick and efficient, and the music is always flowing. It doesn't drag, but it is objectively lengthy at almost three hours, though I saw the second preview so it could tighten up and they could decide to trim it down a bit. Regardless, I quite enjoyed this. The music is great, the choreography, the scenic and lighting design, all very Broadway, vibrant and exciting, and the performances are great too. James Monroe Iglehart is fantastic as Louis. He does a great job emulating Louis’s distinctly brash voice which contrasts nicely with the four women playing his wives. His wives are actually really integral to the story and the structure of the show, and the actresses playing them all have wonderful voices, each with their own unique tone and personality. I think this is what keeps the show from feeling monotonous both musically and narratively, though James Monroe Iglehart certainly deserves a lot of credit for how well he carries such a big show. I don't know if I’d consider this a must-see, but unless you really dislike jazz music for some strange reason, you'll definitely find something to enjoy here. With that, another playbill for my collection.
